{{Quote|My word! This disguise looks quite good on you! I hardly recognized you. This young Rebel is an excellent Jawa ! Don't you agree, Artoo?|C-3PO|<ref name="DW" />}}
During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], an '''undercover agent''' worked for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. Some [[Time/Legends|time]] after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], that agent was as tasked with locating a [[hidden droid factory]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], where the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] had developed a [[Unidentified Imperial assassin droid|new series]] of [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droids]] ready to wreck havoc on [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. To give themselves the means of performing that mission, the agent infiltrated the [[Nkik clan]] of [[Jawa/Legends|Jawa]], learning the art of [[Droid builder/Legends|droid building]] under the aegis of [[Wimateeka]]. The Rebel agent had to equip several droids with the capabilities they needed to meet the challenges of various missions, such as the ability to talk, [[Limb/Legends|arms]] that could manipulate pulleys or enough power to push crates up inclines. After those training missions were completed, the agent recovered a set of [[Optical Information Crystal]]s that revealed the location of the hidden factory. Thanks to a program code reconstructed by putting the crystals' informations together, the Rebel droid builder managed to [[Programmer/Legends|re-program]] the Imperial assassins droids into harmless, dancing ones.

==History==
===Learning the way of the builder===
{{Quote|You have been chosen for a very important mission. But fortunately, we are here to assist you.|C-3PO|<ref name="DW" />}}
At the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], a diminutive [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] served within the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], also know as the Rebel Alliance, a resistance movement that opposed the tyranny of the reigning [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Despite being still [[Youngling/Legends|young]], that individual became one of the Alliance's most trusted secret agents. One [[Standard day/Legends|day]], the [[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance Intelligence]] reported that the Empire had built a secret [[Droid/Legends|droid]] factory somewhere on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], a [[Desert/Legends|desert]], [[Star/Legends|suns]]-scorched [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Arkanis sector/Legends|Arkanis sector]]. They also learnt that Imperial engineers were creating a [[Unidentified Imperial assassin droid|new series]] of [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droids]] in that place. Once completed, those dangerous machines would be released to wreak havoc in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Intent on locating that hidden factory and [[Programmer/Legends|reprogramming]] the droids, the Alliance executive entrusted the diminutive agent with that mission.<ref name="DW" />

The agent was brought to Tatooine aboard a [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]], where they received instructions from [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], a droid duo affiliated with the Alliance heroes [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]. The agent was ordered to pose as a [[Jawa/Legends|Jawa]] so he could gain entrance to the [[Sandcrawler/Legends|sandcrawler]] of the [[Nkik clan]] with the connivance of its leader [[Wimateeka]]. After learning to build droids with the Jawas, the Rebel was tasked with creating a robot that could infiltrate the Imperial factory and reprogram the new assassin droids. To assist them in that mission, the agent teamed up with C-3PO, R2-D2 and [[Cammy]], a chatty [[Holocam E]]-series droid.<ref name="DW" />

With the help of his mechanic partners, the agent learnt the art of droid building in the [[Wimateeka's workshop|workshop]] of Wimateeka, proving worthy of the latter's approval. He or she put newly built droids through a series of tests and maneuvers in the wastes of Tatooine, preparing for the actual infiltration mission. As a first step, the Rebel tested their droids in the [[Sandcrawler Training Facility]]. In that area, the agent could study their new droids' movement, test their speed or their ability to jump, and check if they were magnetic or not.<ref name="DW" />

Following the preliminary test, the Rebel operative began Wimateeka's first training mission. The wheeled droid had to pass through a security exit door located at the top of the cliff in the [[Jundland Wastes/Legends|Jundland Wastes]]. To that end, the droid had to put in place a series of movable enclines by activating switches, taking account of its speed and weight to determine the appropriate slope angle. When the inclines were set, there remained a sizeable gap between the top of the slope and the exit door, which the droid was forced to fill by pushing a wooden crate up the incline. The same mission was repeated once more, although with a legged droid, forcing the droid builder to revise their strategy.<ref name="DW" />

In the second test, the agent had to get a droid across two moving conveyor belts that were used to carry crates containing magnetic items. In order to do so, the builder created a droid that was magnetic itself so it could be pulled off the ground by the trams picking up the crates. Againt, that mission was repeated twice with new objectives. On the second round, the builder's droid was tasked with rescuing a stranded [[R5-series astromech droid]] that had run out of battery power. In order to help the astromech unit, the agent's droid had to pick up a battery located on the other side of the conveyor belts. On the third occurrence of the mission, the agent had to save another stranded droid that needed to be fully re-powered through a power plug and a generator.<ref name="DW" />

===Reprogramming the assassins===
[[File:Droid_builder_award.png|thumb|left|150px|The Rebel agent was awarded a Jawa droid builder certificate.]]
{{Quote|Congratulation for the job well done! You turned all those destructive assassin droids into dancing droids without having to destroy a single one of them!|C-3PO|<ref name="DW" />}}
After a series of supplementary missions during which the Rebel agent learned how to build droid, it became necessary to recover a program code that could render the assassin droids harmless. In order to do so, the agent had to recover several Imperial [[Optical Information Crystal]]s and take them to the [[Jawa Data Crystal Information Area]], where they could be activated with a [[laser light generator]]. One of those crystals was kept in the [[Mos Eisley Salvage Yard/Legends|Mos Eisley Salvage Yard]], another in the [[Phrik metal mine|Phrik Mines]], and the last one was kept by a [[Unidentified moisture farmer (Rebel sympathizer)|moisture farmer]] who supported the Rebel Alliance. While the droid builder had just reconstituted the program code, the Jawas informed them that the Imperial factory had been located in the second quadrant of Tatooine.<ref name="DW" />

Eventually, the The Rebel ended up building their best droid and had it take a disk with with the program code to the hidden factory, the location of which was now known. The robot trespassed into the Imperial factory and reprogrammed the assassin droids into dancing ones. Wimateeka was so proud of his recruit's work that he awarded them with an official [[Jawa droid builder certificate|droid builder certificate]].<ref name="DW" />

==Personality and traits==
The Rebel agent was small enough to go unnoticed amongst the Jawas,<ref name="DW" /> a species whose average height and weight were only one [[Meter/Legends|meter]]<ref name="Databank">{{DB|species|jawa|Jawa}}</ref> and thirty [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]].<ref name="SWHTH">''[[Star Wars: Head-to-Head]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The droid builder was the player character of the ''[[Star Wars: DroidWorks]]'' children-aimed game. The game never specifies the Rebel builder's name or gender, allowing the player to identify themselves with the character. Unlike other game characters&mdash;like [[Rookie One]] from ''[[Star Wars: Rebel Assault]]'' or [[Meetra Surik]] from [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords|''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II'']]&mdash;the Rebel builder has not been reused in later works, and thus was never given a proper canonical identity.

C-3PO comments how the ''young'' Rebel looks good as a Jawa,<ref name="DW" /> which hints this secret operative might have been a child at the time. This seems to be backed up by the droid builder's diminutive height.
